title: How many clicks on a two button calculator reach each number?
description: A calculator has only a plus ten thousand button and a plus one hundred button. Each number is split into ten thousands and hundreds, and the clicks are added. The last number is checked by building it back.
teaching_notes: One idea: use the big button as often as it fits, then the small button for the rest, and add the two counts. Watch for students who forget that a lakh holds ten ten thousands.

source: A calculator has only '+10,000' and '+100' buttons. Write an expression describing the number of button clicks to be made for the following numbers: (a) 20,800 (b) 92,100 (c) 1,20,500 (d) 65,30,000 (e) 70,25,700
video_script.why: The child reads large numbers in lakhs and thousands, and now splits a number into ten thousands and hundreds to count button clicks.
video_script.substitution: Use the big button as many times as it fits, then the small button for the rest; the clicks are the two counts added.
video_script.anchor: a calculator with two buttons, +10,000 and +100, and the five target numbers beside it
video_script.payoff_line: Use the big button as often as it fits, then the small button for the rest

final_answer.spoken: ten, thirty, seventeen, six hundred fifty three and seven hundred fifty nine clicks

maths_rules: 1,20,500 = (12 x 10,000) + (5 x 100); clicks 12 + 5 = 17; one lakh holds ten ten thousands
video_script.design: One idea: big button first, small button for the rest. The calculator stays in the anchor band; the working band shows the splits in three steps and a check. The five numbers are named by their size, not by letters. No hard clear.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>A calculator has only two buttons, plus ten thousand and plus one hundred.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>We want to reach five different numbers.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>For each number, how many clicks are needed?

beats.on_screen: the anchor holds still; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: cards: +10,000 adds 10,000 in 1 click; +100 adds 10,000 only in 100 clicks; the big button saves clicks

marks.m1: the card +10,000 adds 10,000 in 1 click appears
marks.m2: the card +100 adds 10,000 only in 100 clicks appears
marks.m3: the words the big button saves clicks appear

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>One click on the big button adds ten thousand.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>With the small button, adding ten thousand would take one hundred clicks.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The big button saves clicks, so we use it as often as it fits.

marks.m1: the given line is written in the working band

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Given, a calculator with only the plus ten thousand and plus one hundred buttons.

beats.on_screen: To find: the clicks needed for each of the five numbers

marks.m1: the find line is written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We have to find the clicks for each of the five numbers.

marks.m1: the heading big button first appears
marks.m2: 20,800 = (2 x 10,000) + (8 x 100) is written, then clicks 2 + 8 = 10

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, use the big button as many times as it fits.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Twenty thousand eight hundred has two ten thousands and eight hundreds.
That is two plus eight, which is ten clicks.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Ninety two thousand one hundred has nine ten thousands and twenty one hundreds.
That is nine plus twenty one, which is thirty clicks.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, one lakh twenty thousand five hundred.
A lakh holds ten ten thousands.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The number has twelve ten thousands, ten from the lakh and two more, and five hundreds.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>That is twelve plus five, which is seventeen clicks.

marks.m1: the heading the larger numbers appears
marks.m2: 65,30,000 = 653 x 10,000 is written, with nothing left for the small button

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, the larger numbers.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Sixty five lakh thirty thousand is exactly six hundred fifty three ten thousands.
Nothing is left for the small button, so the clicks are six hundred fifty three.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Seventy lakh twenty five thousand seven hundred has seven hundred two ten thousands and fifty seven hundreds.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>That is seven hundred two plus fifty seven, which is seven hundred fifty nine clicks.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, check the last number.
Seven hundred two ten thousands make seventy lakh twenty thousand.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Fifty seven hundreds make five thousand seven hundred.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Together they make seventy lakh twenty five thousand seven hundred.

marks.m2: the five click counts are underlined one by one

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Use the big button as often as it fits, then the small button for the rest.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The five numbers need ten, thirty, seventeen, six hundred fifty three and seven hundred fifty nine clicks.
